final_writeup:
The unrestricted conjecture is not resolved, and no counterexample was found. The strongest new partial conclusion obtained here is:

Theorem. Let G△ be the spanning subgraph of G consisting of the edges that belong to triangles. If G△ is K4-free and 8-degenerate, then τ(G)≤2ν(G). Consequently the inequality holds whenever G△ is K4-free and mad(G△)<9.

This class may have unbounded maximum degree, since an 8-degenerate graph can have unbounded maximum degree. The proof rests on an exact small-link lemma: every triangle-free graph on at most eight vertices is weak König–Egerváry (WKE). The order-eight assertion was verified over all 4,682,270 labelled triangle-free graphs, with a literal WKE witness checked for each.

The induction is explicit. If the link of v has a WKE witness (M,Q), use the triangles vxy for xy∈M as a packing and delete M together with the spokes vq for q∈Q. This costs at most twice the packing size, kills every triangle through v, and makes the packing compatible with the residual graph. In a K4-free 8-degenerate graph, every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most eight, and its link is triangle-free, so the small-link lemma applies recursively.

The finite threshold is sharp for this method. Blow up the vertices of C5 into independent parts of sizes (1,2,2,2,2), joining consecutive parts completely. The resulting nine-vertex graph is triangle-free but not WKE. Thus K4-freeness alone cannot extend the same singleton-link argument from degree eight to degree nine. This graph is not claimed to be a counterexample to Tuza's inequality.

Two further extensions follow. Every locally bipartite graph satisfies Tuza's inequality, without a degree restriction. Also, packing and covering are additive over the edge-overlap components of the triangle family. Hence it suffices that each such triangle component is either locally bipartite or K4-free and 8-degenerate.

The source also states results for maximum degree at most seven and maximum average degree below seven. They are not included in the independently established componentwise theorem here: the first depends on an external catalogue of 1,144 certificates and verifiers absent from the authorized evidence, and the second is cited without its proof.

Accordingly, any subgraph-minimal K4-free counterexample to Tuza's conjecture would have every edge in a triangle, only one triangle-overlap component, minimum degree at least nine, and maximum average degree at least nine. The explicit nine-vertex non-WKE graph shows why further progress requires more than the present singleton reduction.

results.claim: A WKE link gives a self-contained one-vertex reduction.
results.proof_sketch: Let H=G[N(v)] have a matching M and a set Q with |Q|≤|M| such that Q covers H−M. Put S={vxy:xy∈M} and X=M∪{vq:q∈Q}. Since M is a matching, S is edge-disjoint. Also |X|=|M|+|Q|≤2|S|. Every triangle vxy is hit: either xy∈M⊆X, or xy∈E(H)−M and one of x,y lies in Q. The only S-edges avoiding v are the edges of M, all in X. For G'=(G−X)−v, a packing in G' is edge-disjoint from S, while X together with a transversal of G' covers G. Hence τ(G')≤2ν(G') implies τ(G)≤2ν(G).

results.claim: Every graph whose every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link satisfies τ≤2ν.
results.proof_sketch: Induct on the number of vertices. Choose the guaranteed vertex v and apply the WKE-link reduction. Its residual G' is a proper subgraph. Every subgraph of G' is also a subgraph of G, so the hypothesis is inherited. Induction gives the inequality for G', and the reduction gives it for G.

results.claim: Every locally bipartite graph satisfies τ≤2ν.
results.proof_sketch: Here locally bipartite means that G[N(v)] is bipartite for every v. This property is inherited by arbitrary subgraphs. Every bipartite graph is König–Egerváry and hence WKE: take a maximum matching and a vertex cover of the same size. Thus every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link, and the preceding elimination theorem applies.

results.claim: Every triangle-free graph on at most eight vertices is WKE.
results.proof_sketch: The checker generated labelled triangle-free graphs recursively: when adjoining a vertex, its old neighbor set ranges over exactly the independent sets of the old graph. Thus every labelled triangle-free graph appears exactly once. For each of the 4,682,270 order-eight graphs it enumerated Q with |Q|≤4. The edges induced by V−Q are forced into M; the checker required those edges to be a matching, extended them to a matching of size at least |Q|, and then literally verified M⊆E(H), that M is a matching, and that Q covers H−M. Every graph passed. Smaller orders follow either from the separate exhaustive check or by padding with isolated vertices and then removing isolates from Q.

results.claim: The order-eight WKE bound is sharp: a triangle-free non-WKE graph exists on nine vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Let H be the blow-up of C5 with independent cyclic parts A0,…,A4 of sizes 1,2,2,2,2 and all edges between consecutive parts. It is triangle-free. If R induces maximum degree at most one, write ri=|R∩Ai|. If some ri=2, then r_{i−1}=r_{i+1}=0; the remaining two parts are consecutive and contribute at most two vertices, so |R|≤4. If every ri≤1, selecting five vertices selects every part and gives each selected vertex two neighbors, again impossible. Thus |R|≤4. In a WKE witness (M,Q), |M|≤4 and hence |V(H)−Q|≥5. Every edge induced outside Q would have to belong to M, making that induced graph a matching, contradiction.

results.claim: Deleting every edge that lies in no triangle preserves both ν and τ.
results.proof_sketch: Let G△ contain exactly the triangle-edges of G. Every triangle of G has all three edges in G△, while every triangle of G△ is already a triangle of G. Thus the two graphs have identical triangle families. Packings are therefore identical, and a transversal never needs an edge outside G△, giving ν(G△)=ν(G) and τ(G△)=τ(G).

results.claim: Triangle packing and covering are additive over triangle edge-overlap components.
results.proof_sketch: Declare two triangles equivalent when they are joined by a chain in which consecutive triangles share an edge. Let Gi be the support graph formed by the edges of one equivalence class. Distinct Gi have disjoint edge sets; otherwise triangles from two classes containing a common edge would be equivalent. Consequently maximum packings combine independently, and every transversal restricts to a transversal in each Gi. Hence ν(G)=Σiν(Gi) and τ(G)=Σiτ(Gi), after ignoring edges in no triangle.

results.claim: If the triangle-edge subgraph G△ is K4-free and 8-degenerate, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
results.proof_sketch: It suffices to prove the assertion for G△. Every nonempty subgraph J of G△ has a vertex v with dJ(v)≤8. Since J is K4-free, J[NJ(v)] is triangle-free: a triangle in that link together with v would be a K4. The small-link lemma makes this link WKE. Thus G△ satisfies the WKE-elimination criterion, proving τ(G△)≤2ν(G△). Triangle-edge pruning transfers the inequality back to G.

results.claim: If G△ is K4-free and mad(G△)<9, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
results.proof_sketch: Every nonempty subgraph of G△ has average degree below nine and therefore has a vertex of integer degree at most eight. Hence G△ is 8-degenerate, and the preceding theorem applies.

results.claim: A subgraph-minimal K4-free counterexample would have every edge in a triangle and minimum degree at least nine.
results.proof_sketch: An edge in no triangle could be deleted without changing ν or τ, contradicting minimality. If some vertex v had degree at most eight, its link would be triangle-free on at most eight vertices and hence WKE. The WKE-link reduction would reduce the assertion to a proper subgraph, which satisfies Tuza’s inequality by minimality, again a contradiction. Thus δ(G)≥9, so mad(G)≥9. Triangle-component additivity additionally permits choosing such a counterexample with only one triangle edge-overlap component.

results.claim: The inequality holds componentwise whenever every triangle edge-overlap component has either a locally bipartite structure or a K4-free 8-degenerate structure.
results.proof_sketch: Triangle-component additivity makes componentwise assembly valid. The locally bipartite theorem and the K4-free 8-degenerate theorem establish τ≤2ν for the two respective component classes. Apply the appropriate theorem to each component and sum the resulting inequalities. No Δ≤7 or mad<7 alternative is asserted because the authorized evidence does not contain an independently checkable proof of those source-dependent branches.
